title: The hero who endured twenty years of attacks: Han Hong, not Luo Yonghao
dek: Luo Yonghao admits that being questioned about water bottle brands during charity work nearly broke him. He calls Han Hong—who withstood twenty years of allegations and attacks—a true hero he could never be.
why: Most of the episode is banter about hair loss, OCD, and ADHD. The second half contains the only substantive content: Luo Yonghao discussing Wenchuan earthquake charity accounting and his assessment of Han Hong.
who: Audiences who enjoy comedians trading quips, are curious about ADHD and OCD self-diagnosis, or want to hear Luo Yonghao rarely speak seriously about charity work.
skip: Skip the banter about hair loss, ADHD, and OCD—low information density. The core content is the charity discussion after 2:07.

points.h: Hair loss is not a vanity issue—it is a camera exposure problem
points.body: Camera operators use hairline powder and require darker skin to solve overexposure issues caused by reflection off the scalp. It is a technical constraint, not a cosmetic one.

points.h: ADHD is not an inability to focus—it is a different kind of switch
points.body: Luo uses four monitors—two for focused work, all four for open-ended thinking. He would use sixteen if possible, but is limited by Mac Studio's 4 Thunderbolt ports. His ADHD is not an inability to focus but a different activation pattern; the switch is simply set differently than others'.

points.h: ADHD's true cost: arriving late to major launches, even willing to refund tickets
points.body: Luo never misses weekly company meetings, but always arrives late to major launches with thousands of attendees—sometimes by over an hour, requiring ticket refunds. Event size directly triggers ADHD symptoms. The severity of lateness shows the condition's grip increases with pressure and stakes.

points.h: OCD runs on invisible labor no one else can see
points.body: OCD sufferers maintain invisible order that others never notice. All his airplane models face the same 45-degree angle. If someone moves one and dusts it, he can instantly spot something is wrong—the only person aware of the displacement.

points.h: OCD's hoarding compulsion: taking responsibility for a piece of paper from creation to trash
points.body: He collects discarded namecards and materials from events, keeping them in desk drawers. Once paper is printed and used, he feels obligated to save it from becoming garbage. He would not feel this responsibility for paper bearing Luo Yonghao's name, only for paper over which he holds stewardship.

points.h: Naming locations in sensational content brings harassment; anonymity becomes accidental tourism promotion
points.body: A comedian who named his hometown got doxxed with specific addresses and floor numbers; neighbors grew angry and the reaction only faded with time. Another who obscured all locations using province codes and generic regions ended up with locals treating his stories as tourism marketing. Same content type; opposite outcomes based solely on naming practice.

points.h: Luo Yonghao: disputes over water bottle brands nearly destroyed his charity work
points.body: During Wenchuan earthquake relief, Luo organized donations and did hand accounting every night. Dozens to hundreds of yuan always went unaccounted for, which he covered himself. After publishing the data, supporters pressured him about water bottle brands. This line of questioning nearly broke him emotionally. By contrast, Han Hong has endured twenty years of allegations and attacks while maintaining her charity work—which Luo calls heroic in a way he admits he could never manage.

points.h: Hair transplant doctors call any transplantable hair outside the scalp 'resources'
points.body: In industry jargon, transplantable hair and body hair reserves are called 'resources,' including beard hair and leg hair. These grafted hairs retain their original growth characteristics from their source location. A colleague had scalp hair transplanted into his eyebrows; the hair kept growing indefinitely without requiring trimming, alarming his wife.

terms.def: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a neurodevelopmental condition affecting the ability to sustain attention or maintain focus, not synonymous with restlessness or an inability to sit still.

quotes.text: So I came up with a solution: get a bowl, fill it with hairline powder, and I can dip into it like you dip hot-pot sauce—haha—just paint it on in a circle.
If this interface had no limits, I'd be like a security guard staring at sixteen screens, making sure they're all covered with densely packed Wikipedia pages so I can read the titles clearly.

For example, I'm never late to our weekly company meetings. But if I organize a big launch event with twelve thousand people—and we're selling tickets—I will absolutely be late taking the stage. Twenty minutes, thirty minutes, sometimes an hour—I'd rather refund tickets.
I have lots of airplane models. All facing the same angle—45 degrees, with wings lined up. If someone moves one and dusts it off, I can always tell something is wrong.

We with OCD have this particularly primal, authentic impulse: to take ultimate responsibility for everything. If a name is printed on paper and it's been used, I alone must be responsible for it. If I don't manage this paper, nobody else will care about it. The staff will just throw it away and it becomes garbage. Luo Yonghao would never feel responsible for paper bearing his own name, but I do—because this paper has borne my intentions, served its purpose, and I must answer for it.
So he's been doing charity for nearly twenty years, constantly attacked and smeared, but he persists anyway. That's a true hero. I could never do that.
